descriptionChirho: The wrongful act itself — moral perversity, crookedness, or transgression against God's standard; the dominant sense of עָוֹן covering the vast majority of occurrences across all grammatical forms (singular/plural, all pronominal suffixes, construct chains, and prepositional prefixes).

The state of being guilty or culpable before God — the objective liability that attaches to the sinner after committing עָוֹן; distinguished by English 'guilt', Swahili 'hatia' (guilt), and contexts where the focus is on the condition rather than the act or its consequence.

The punishment or penalty visited upon the sinner as consequence of עָוֹן — distinguished by English 'punishment', Korean 벌 (beol), Swahili 'adhabu' (punishment), and Spanish 'castigo'; prominent in the idiom נשׂא עון when the subject endures the penalty rather than forgives it.

Rare alternative reading where עָוֹן is interpreted as affliction or misery rather than iniquity, possibly reflecting confusion with עֳנִי or a deliberate repointing; attested in Lamentations-type contexts where translators render 'my affliction' rather than 'my iniquity'.

Anomalous occurrence where translators render עָוֹן as 'eyeing' or 'hostile' (Arabic مُعادٍ, Korean 원수 = enemy, Swahili 'akiwa macho'), likely reflecting a textual or semantic confusion with עַיִן (eye) or a rare metaphorical extension; may belong to a different lemma entirely.
